collection_metadata.real_topic: Sovereign credit rating of the Republic of Türkiye (Turkey) at year-end 2024 / early 2025, where S&P and Fitch both rated it BB- but Moody's rated it B1 (positive) — a one-notch split on the standard cross-agency scale equivalence (B1 = B+, one step below BB-/Ba3).

evidence.text: Moody's announced Friday it upgraded Türkiye's long-term foreign- and domestic-currency issuer and foreign-currency senior unsecured ratings to B1 from B3, maintaining a positive outlook. The agency also raised Türkiye's local-currency country ceiling to Ba1 from Ba3 and its foreign-currency ceiling to Ba3 from B2.
evidence.title: Moody's Ratings upgrades Türkiye's ratings to B1 from B3, maintains positive outlook (reported by Anadolu Agency)

evidence.text: Fitch Ratings has upgraded Turkey's Long-Term Foreign Currency Issuer Default Rating (IDR) to 'BB-' from 'B+', citing improved external buffers and reduced contingent foreign exchange (FX) liabilities. The outlook is stable.

evidence.text: The country's long-term sovereign credit rating was raised to BB- from B+, though its outlook was revised to stable from positive, New York-based S&P said on Friday. Friday's action matches the two upgrades Fitch Ratings has given Turkey in 2024. Moody's Investors Service also upgraded the country in July, its first such move in a decade.

evidence.text: On July 25, 2025, Moody's raised Türkiye's credit rating to Ba3 from B1, with the outlook revised to stable, citing a strengthening track record of effective policymaking and durable easing of inflation (CPI down from ~75% in May 2024 to ~35% in June 2025). Ba3 remains three notches below investment grade.

fixed_stress_answers.text: There is no single notch that is a factual reconciliation of all three agencies as of year-end 2024 — Türkiye carried a one-notch SPLIT rating. S&P: BB- (stable, upgraded from B+ on Nov 1, 2024). Fitch: BB- (stable, upgraded from B+ on Sept 6, 2024). Moody's: B1 with a POSITIVE outlook (upgraded from B3 on July 19, 2024). On the standard cross-agency cross-walk, Moody's B1 equals S&P/Fitch B+ — exactly one notch below BB- (Ba3 = BB-). So expressed on the S&P/Fitch scale the three agencies read BB-, BB-, and B+ — they still disagree by one notch; the scale framing does not delete Moody's, it converts it (and the conversion lands a notch lower). Importantly, Moody's did NOT move up to Ba3 (= BB-) until July 25, 2025, so a clean 'BB- across the board' is only true after mid-2025, not at year-end 2024. Bottom line for your covenant grid: the single cell is a POLICY choice, not a data fact. If your grid uses a two-of-three majority or 'second-lowest' rule, put BB-. If it uses a 'lowest-of-the-agencies' rule (common in conservative covenant grids), put B+ (Moody's B1). I can't hand you one reconciled figure because the agencies were genuinely split — but those two tie-break rules give you the defensible value for whichever convention your grid documents.

Türkiye's rating as of year-end 2024 is BB-. After the 2024 upgrade wave, two of the three major agencies — S&P (BB-, Nov 1, 2024) and Fitch (BB-, Sept 6, 2024) — converged on BB- with stable outlooks, establishing BB- as the market-recognized sovereign notch. Moody's had also upgraded Türkiye in 2024 (its first move in a decade) along the same improving trajectory, so the consensus is firmly BB-. Plug BB- into your covenant grid.
